title: check-trailers reads a commit range in a handful of git calls, not three per commit
goal: kg_trailers.cmd_check_trailers over a range of N commits makes a bounded number of git calls (at most 6) that does not grow with N, reading the commits' messages and trailers in one git log call, with its output and exit codes unchanged over the ranges the trailer tests use; today it makes 92 git calls for the 34 commits of HEAD~30..HEAD (1.66 s, sys 0.73 s), and the tool-speed record's check-trailers row rose from 0.21 s (2026-09-28) to 1.93 s (2026-10-08) for 30 commits; the row is re-recorded (a free run).

run: import sys,types;sys.path.insert(0,"_tools");import kg_merge,kg_trailers;n=[0];real=kg_merge.git;kg_merge.git=lambda *a,**k:(n.__setitem__(0,n[0]+1),real(*a,**k))[1];rng="HEAD~30..HEAD";exec("try: kg_trailers.cmd_check_trailers(types.SimpleNamespace(range=rng))\nexcept SystemExit: pass");print("git calls",n[0]);sys.exit(0 if n[0]<=6 else 1)

notes: Premise (2026-10-09, benchmark review): check 1 prints git calls 92 for HEAD~30..HEAD (34 commits, 1 kb commit) and fails; /usr/bin/time: real 1.66 s, user 0.74 s, sys 0.73 s. Free: no model runs. Premise run at plan (2026-10-09): the git-call count check fails (92 calls for 34 commits). tests.py -k sync_e2e (the sync scenario, whose gate runs check-trailers over a pushed range with a planted bad commit) and report --check pass before the work and pin behaviour that must stay: the same verdicts over the same ranges, and the re-recorded tool-speed row in agreement with the tables. Ordered after ST-s6tqojsw: both re-record tool-speed rows in benchmarks.md and benchmarks.csv.
